Anyway, here's some tips from that time when I lost 20 kg over 2 months (85 kg to 65 kg at 6").

If you want to lose your excess weight in a reasonable amount of time, you'll need to drastically cut your food intake. As a matter of fact, I found that even eating one meal a day, I was just about maintaining my weight at about 80-85 kg. Faced between the option of consistently reducing my meal portions, I simply chose the easier option of intermittent fasting, where I would go several days to a week without food and then have a day or two where I would maintain my weight and reassess my body (note that your body begins to change slowly from your mental image as your approach a BMI of 26-27 as your belly fat starts disappearing, then more rapidly as muscles start to show. The abs are generally the first to show, followed by your other muscles and tendons (at about BMI 23-24). Also, I made a point of weighing myself everyday to see how rapidly I could lose the weight, which was enough motivation in itself.

From my experience, I was able to consistently lose 0.5-0.8kg per day when I was not eating, depending on my activity level. Then, on days when I ate, my weight stayed more or less the same to within 0.2kg. After about a month or two, my weight reached 67 kg and I decided to halt the intermittent fasting and go back to a meal a day (both for ease of portion control and convenience). Then it was just a matter of slowly reducing the frequency of weighings as I began increasingly confident in judging my portion size.
